claims.text: Increasing atomic size mismatch in equiatomic refractory HEAs enhances lattice distortion.
Enhanced lattice distortion creates larger local stress fields.
Larger local stress fields impede dislocation motion.
Greater resistance to dislocation motion increases high-temperature yield strength.
Enhanced lattice distortion modifies the elastic lattice response.
Enhanced lattice distortion changes the balance between plastic deformation and elastic recovery.
Changes in the balance between plastic deformation and elastic recovery modify thermoelastic response at high temperature.
Equiatomic WNbMoTa is presented as an example baseline refractory HEA with minimal atomic size mismatch.
Slight compositional substitutions can be designed to increase atomic size mismatch while processing history is held constant.
XRD line broadening and local strain-field characterization can measure the degree of lattice distortion.
The higher-mismatch variant is predicted to have greater measured lattice distortion than the baseline.
The higher-mismatch variant is predicted to have higher yield strength than the baseline at approximately 1500°C.
The higher-mismatch variant is predicted to have a modified elastic modulus relative to the baseline.
The higher-mismatch variant is predicted to exhibit a measurable difference in recoverable thermoelastic strain amplitude relative to the baseline.
The proposed relationship is expected to apply near 1500°C under controlled atmospheres and identical processing histories apart from composition.
